Python API Reference#

High-level Python API for the ovphysx library.

Stream-Ordered Execution Model#

Operations on each instance execute in submission order. Submission may execute inline; the task contract still separates admission from completion:

  • Operations appear to complete in submission order

  • Writes from operation N are visible to operation N+1

  • Wait for a creator before passing its output handle to another operation

  • Independent operations may execute concurrently internally for performance

Example using the explicit synchronous read convenience:

Listing 1 Stream-ordered operation sequence#
 from ovphysx.types import ObjectScope, SimObjectType

 def step_and_read(physx, stage, initial_ordinal, from_ordinal, to_ordinal, dt):
     physx.wait_task(physx.attach_ovstage(stage, read_ordinal=initial_ordinal))
     # After the application authors later ovstage edits:
     physx.wait_task(physx.update_from_ovstage(from_ordinal, to_ordinal))
     physx.step(dt)  # Sees the drained stage edits
     with physx.read_sync(
         SimObjectType.RIGID_BODY, ["position"], scope=ObjectScope.ALL
     ) as result:  # Reads current state
         for group in result.groups:
             for tensor in group.tensors:
                 print(tensor.numpy())

Use Operation.wait(), wait_task(), or wait_all() when:

  • Before materializing an operation’s typed result

  • To ensure operations complete before program exit

  • For explicit synchronization points in your application

Host task collection and CUDA stream dependencies are separate. Materializing a read group orders its producer event onto the current Warp stream. A write commit’s stream and event describe the caller’s producer completion; they do not select the stream PhysX uses for its own work.

Thread Safety#

  • Each instance holds at most one live ovstage attach. Several instances may be attached at once, and attaching one does not detach another. The same ovstage instance cannot be attached to two PhysX instances.

  • Different instances may step their own attachments at the same time. A single instance is NOT thread-safe. Use external synchronization if calling from multiple threads on the same instance.

  • Process-wide limits still apply: one hard CPU-only mode, one SDK tolerance scale, and a recording start/stop that needs every attached instance idle.

  • ctypes releases the GIL during native calls, so concurrent step() and PhysX.read() / PhysX.write() from different threads on the same instance is a data race. See the developer guide threading section for the recommended pattern.

Core Classes#

class ovphysx.api.PhysX(
*,
config: PhysXConfig | None = None,
ignore_version_mismatch: bool = False,
active_cuda_gpus: str | None = None,
)#

Bases: object

High-level wrapper around the C API using ctypes.

attach_ovstage(
stage,
*,
read_ordinal: int = 1,
) → Task#

Attach an ovstage Stage and return its Task receipt.

Attach performs the initial scene parse at read_ordinal. After the producer authors later ovstage edits, call update_from_ovstage() with only those subsequent ordinals. Tensor bindings remain available as a perf escape hatch.

Execution currently runs inline. Collect the returned Task with wait_task() or wait_all() before using the attachment; accepted execution failures are reported by that wait.

Parameters:

  • stage – An owner-aware ovstage.Stage; raw pointers are a low-level C integration.

  • read_ordinal – Caller-owned ovstage ordinal at which selected physics data is sealed. Must be non-zero. 0 is reserved as the runtime skip-cursor sentinel. The application owns ordinal advancement. Defaults to 1. open_usd() / population does not seal data, so call advance_write_floor() first. Attachment fails if the initial articulation/joint schema scan cannot read that ordinal.

Preconditions:

  • Instance must be valid.

  • Not already attached to a Stage.

  • No other instance is required to detach first. Several instances may be attached at once. This call does not detach them.

  • Selected physics data must be sealed at read_ordinal.

  • read_ordinal must be non-zero.

  • The application registered the codeless PhysX schemas with ovstage before the first USD schema read, including population or export, in each process and worker, using both resource directories from the separately installed physx-usd-schemas provider (see the samples). Population drops attributes of schemas it cannot resolve. If ovstage reports that either physxSchema or omniUsdPhysicsDeformableSchema was missing when its USD schema registry was built, the native guard rejects admission and this method raises RuntimeError before returning a Task or taking Stage ownership. The refusal persists for the process: restart and register before populating or exporting. A procedural Stage attached while USD schema definitions remain unbuilt skips the family check, leaving it active for later attaches. Once population or export builds the definitions, even procedural Stages are checked. Registration another USD consumer made unobservable to ovstage cannot be detected. Nor can the guard identify schema families registered late before its first check: catching a late registration’s OvstageError can let a later attach succeed with missing data. Always restart after a registration-ordering error; successful attach does not prove schema availability during population. The legacy setting /ovphysx/schemas/requireRegistration defaults to true; setting it to false with PhysXConfig(carbonite_overrides=...) permits attach with a warning but does not repair lost data.

  • Scenes that author Newton newton:* attributes need the Newton USD schema (pip install newton-usd-schemas) registered in the same call (ovphysx.newton_schema_root()); population drops those attributes otherwise. Before the native attach this call checks the installed package’s registration once per process and emits a RuntimeWarning if ovstage reports late registration; a warning promoted to an error therefore leaves the instance detached. When the package is not installed it logs a warning on the ovphysx logger instead (nothing is wrong for scenes without newton:* attributes, and suites that promote warnings to errors stay unaffected). The check probes only once USD has built its schema definitions, including through export. A procedurally authored stage attached while those definitions remain unbuilt is left alone, so the check never registers a schema on the application’s behalf. It recognizes the Newton schema family registered from any complete copy. The setting /ovphysx/schemas/warnMissingNewtonSchema = false (PhysXConfig(carbonite_overrides=...), "false" accepted) silences the check, for a registration ovstage cannot observe. This Newton check does not check either PhysX schema family; silencing it does not bypass the native PhysX registration guard.

Lifetime:

  • stage must outlive the attachment because ovphysx captures and dereferences its native pointer until detach. This wrapper holds a reference to stage for the duration of the attachment, so a Stage created inline (attach_ovstage(ovstage.Stage(...))) stays alive. The reference is held from module scope, so garbage collection of an unreachable cycle containing this instance cannot finalize the Stage before the instance’s teardown detaches it. The reference survives pending or failed teardown, and is dropped when a lifecycle task is collected and native ownership has ended, or by destroy().

Returns:

Immutable Task receipt. Its SUCCESS status means admission only.

Errors:

  • Raises TypeError if stage is not an owner-aware ovstage.Stage, including None or a raw native handle.

  • Propagates ovstage.OvstageError if stage was destroyed.

  • Raises ValueError if read_ordinal is 0.

  • Raises RuntimeError if this instance is already attached, the Stage’s native handle is null, the native PhysX schema guard refuses the process, or submission is otherwise rejected. A schema refusal creates no Task and changes no attachment.

  • Accepted execution failures raise TaskError when collected. Failed rollback can leave an attachment; use is_stage_attached() after collection to check ownership. A peer instance’s attachment is left in place.

clone(
source_path: str,
target_paths: list[str],
anchor_transforms: list[tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float, float]] | None = None,
env_ids: list[int] | None = None,
) → Task#

Clone a prim hierarchy to create multiple runtime physics copies.

Creates physics-optimized clones in the runtime representation for high-performance simulation, backed by the PhysX SDK replicator so cloned articulations are real articulations. The source prim must exist in the loaded stage and have physics properties. Replication executes inline. The returned Task is already complete. On success subsequent operations see the clone immediately. Accepted execution failures are reported by wait_task() or wait_all(); the receipt’s SUCCESS status describes admission, not execution.

This is the clone entrypoint for both standalone callers and callers that populate the scene through an ovstage Stage attached via attach_ovstage(). Replication runs in the internal representation only (USD untouched).

Cross-environment collision filtering can optionally use PhysX environment ids, controlled by the /ovphysx/clone/useEnvIds setting (default: on). When enabled and the scene runs GPU dynamics + GPU broadphase, each cloned environment gets a distinct environment id so copies in different environments do not collide. The source environment is included: its bodies are created holding environment id 0 (assigned as the attach parses them; clones get 1..N), so co-located clones (anchor_transforms=None) are collision-isolated from the source as well. Environment ids do not provide collision isolation in CPU mode. Give CPU clones spatially disjoint anchor_transforms. Otherwise all copies share one collision space. The runtime logs a warning when env ids are requested but GPU dynamics or GPU broadphase is unavailable. Call ovphysx.enable_python_logging() to receive it on the ovphysx Python logger. Like all carbonite settings, useEnvIds is per-process (shared by every ovphysx instance in the process), so set it consistently before attaching.

When one logical environment is assembled from SEVERAL clone calls (e.g. an IsaacLab ClonePlan cloning one source row at a time: first /env0/Robot to every environment, then /env0/Object), pass env_ids so objects that share an environment share an environment id. With env_ids=None each call numbers its copies afresh, so /env1/Robot and /env1/Object cloned by different calls would land on different ids and never collide with each other:

def clone_environment_parts(physx):
    env_ids = [0, 1]  # same ids in every call -> same environments
    physx.clone("/env0/Robot", ["/env1/Robot", "/env2/Robot"], env_ids=env_ids)
    physx.clone("/env0/Object", ["/env1/Object", "/env2/Object"], env_ids=env_ids)
    physx.wait_all()
Parameters:

  • source_path – USD path of the source prim hierarchy to clone (e.g., “/World/env0”)

  • target_paths – Runtime physics-object paths for the cloned hierarchies (e.g., [“/World/env1”, “/World/env2”])

  • anchor_transforms – Optional list of (px, py, pz, qx, qy, qz, qw) transforms giving the absolute world pose of each target subtree root. Entry i anchors the exact subtree at target_paths[i]. Position is followed by quaternion rotation (imaginary-first, matching tensor API convention). Identity rotation = (0, 0, 0, 1). Must have the same length as target_paths. Descendants keep their poses relative to the source subtree root: target_object_world = anchor_transforms[i] * inverse(source_root_world) * source_object_world. Pass None to co-locate every copy on the source. Co-location is collision-isolated only under GPU dynamics + GPU broadphase. In CPU mode, provide spatially disjoint transforms to avoid cross-environment collisions.

  • env_ids – Optional logical environment id per target (list of int, same length as target_paths, each 0 <= id < 0x00FFFFFF, because PhysX supports at most 1<<24 environments and the runtime id is env_ids[i] + 1). Stable across calls: the same id always maps to the same runtime environment, so clones from different calls that share an id collide with each other and stay isolated from every other environment (engages under GPU dynamics + GPU broadphase, like all env-id filtering). Pass None for automatic per-call numbering (each call’s copies get fresh ids past every previous call’s).

Returns:

Immutable Task receipt for use with wait_task().

Raises:

  • ValueError – If paths are invalid, anchor_transforms has the wrong length or contains an invalid pose, or env_ids has the wrong length or contains an invalid id.

  • RuntimeError – If clone fails to queue, if no ovstage Stage is attached, or if clone() is called after warmup() or the first step() / step_sync(). Cloning after warmup corrupts simulation state on GPU and is rejected in all modes for API consistency. To recover, call detach_ovstage(), wait for it to complete, then reload the source scene or reattach its ovstage before cloning again.

Preconditions:

  • An ovstage Stage is attached and source_path names physics to clone.

  • target_paths are unique and do not already exist.

  • warmup() has not been called and no step() / step_sync() has run since the current stage was attached.

Side effects:

  • Creates live PhysX objects keyed by the target paths. No USD or runtime-stage prims are authored.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • Clones remain valid until detach_ovstage().

Threading:

  • Do not call concurrently on the same instance without external sync.

Errors:

  • Raises ValueError for invalid inputs.

  • Raises RuntimeError when submission is rejected, including duplicate-target and after-step/after-warmup ordering violations.

  • Accepted execution failures raise TaskError when collected by a wait.

create_contact_binding(
sensor_patterns: list[str],
filter_patterns: list[str] | None = None,
filters_per_sensor: int = 0,
max_contact_data_count: int = 0,
) → ContactBinding#

Create a contact binding for reading aggregate and detailed contact tensors.

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: Contact bindings are deprecated.

Returns DLPack-compatible tensors of net forces [S, 3] or force matrices [S, F, 3]. Detailed contact and friction data are exposed as flat [C, ...] buffers plus [S, F] count/start-index tensors via ContactBinding.read_normal_contact_data() and ContactBinding.read_friction_contact_data().

A sensor is a set of rigid bodies matched by a physics-object path pattern. A filter is a second set of bodies whose contacts with each sensor you want to measure. Patterns include authored USD objects and runtime-only clones.

Sensor selection is opt-in: every authored USD prim matched by sensor_patterns must have PhysxContactReportAPI applied, on the prim named as the sensor itself (not a parent body or child collider). A matched prim without the schema is dropped from the binding, and if that leaves no sensors this call raises RuntimeError. Filter prims need no extra schema. Runtime-only clones use the schema metadata copied from the corresponding source object: a cloned collider whose source collider lacks the schema is rejected even if its parent body has it.

On CPU simulation and GPU dynamics with CPU readback, a separate child collider’s schema enables sensor selection, not reporting for its owning body. Also enable reporting on the body, owning articulation link, or articulation root to avoid depending on reports from the other actor in each pair. If neither actor reports matching contacts, the child sensor reads zero. Configure reporting settings on the reporting actor or articulation root; a standalone static collider is its own actor.

In these modes, enable owner reporting but select only the child as a binding sensor. If the owner is also selected as a sensor in this or another live contact binding on the same attachment, the owner takes precedence: contacts are credited to the owner and the child reads zero. Check wildcard patterns for unintended owner matches, and establish bindings before stepping. Session reads support selecting both the owner and child in these modes.

On DirectGPU, a separate child collider carrying PhysxContactReportAPI is accepted by the deprecated contact binding, but the runtime logs an unsupported collider warning and the child reads zero force. DirectGPU session queries omit that child row; select the owning body or articulation link instead.

The binding must be created before the first simulation step whose contacts you want to observe. Call ContactBinding.read_net_normal_forces() or ContactBinding.read_normal_force_matrix() after a successful PhysX.step() or PhysX.step_sync() call. Before the first step, both return all-zeros tensors.

Result tensor shapes after step:

  • net forces: [S, 3] where S = matched sensor count

  • force matrix: [S, F, 3] where F = matched filter count per sensor

  • detailed data: flat [C, 1] or [C, 3] buffers indexed by counts and start_indices with shape [S, F]

Use ContactBinding.sensor_paths and ContactBinding.filter_paths to map rows and columns back to resolved physics-object paths.

Example:

import torch

def read_contact_forces(physx):
    with physx.create_contact_binding(
        sensor_patterns=["/World/robot_0/ee"],
        filter_patterns=["/World/obstacles/box"],
        filters_per_sensor=1,
        max_contact_data_count=256,
    ) as binding:
        # Call this after a successful simulation step.
        forces = torch.zeros(
            (binding.sensor_count, 3), device="cuda"
        )
        binding.read_net_normal_forces(forces)
        return forces
Parameters:

  • sensor_patterns – Physics-object path patterns for sensor bodies. A single path component may be at most 4096 characters long; a longer one raises RuntimeError (also for filter_patterns). The matching rules are on the “Path patterns” page of the ovphysx documentation.

  • filter_patterns – Flat list of physics-object path patterns for filters. Total length must equal len(sensor_patterns) * filters_per_sensor. Pass None with filters_per_sensor=0 to get contacts with all bodies.

  • filters_per_sensor – Number of filter patterns per sensor (same for all sensors).

  • max_contact_data_count – Max raw contact pairs to track in the native backend. Also caps the detailed contact/friction flat-buffer reads. Detailed reads require this value and filters_per_sensor to be positive.

create_sdf_view(
pattern: str,
max_query_points: int,
) → SdfView#

Create an SDF shape view for evaluating signed distance fields.

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: SDF views are deprecated. Use evaluate_sdf_shapes(), which evaluates the same shapes through an SDF_SHAPE output query and takes Q from the arrays on every call.

Requires a GPU instance. CPU SDF evaluation is not implemented.

Parameters:

  • pattern – Physics-object path pattern matching SDF collision shapes, including runtime-only clones. A single path component may be at most 4096 characters long; a longer one raises RuntimeError. The matching rules are on the “Path patterns” page of the ovphysx documentation.

  • max_query_points – Number of query points per shape per call. Query tensors passed to SdfView.evaluate must have Q equal to this.

Returns:

SdfView with count == number of matched shapes.

Example:

sdf = physx.create_sdf_view("/World/Mesh*", max_query_points=64)
# Query/output tensors must be on the CUDA device (SDF eval is GPU-only).
pts = torch.zeros((sdf.count, 64, 3), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
out = torch.zeros((sdf.count, 64, 4), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
sdf.evaluate(pts, out)
sdf.destroy()
create_tensor_binding(
pattern: str = None,
prim_paths: list[str] = None,
tensor_type: int = TensorType.RIGID_BODY_POSE,
*,
raise_if_empty: bool = False,
) → TensorBinding#

Create tensor binding for bulk physics data access (synchronous).

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The tensor-binding API is deprecated. Use PhysX.read() for reads and PhysX.write() for writes.

A tensor binding connects physics objects (by path pattern or explicit paths) to a tensor type, including authored USD objects and runtime-only clones.

Parameters:

  • pattern – Physics-object path pattern (e.g., “/World/robot*”, “/World/env[0-9]/robot”; [N] is not an index placeholder, it matches the letter N). The matching rules are on the “Path patterns” page of the ovphysx documentation. A single path component (the text between two slashes; a parenthesized group counts as one component even if it contains a slash) may be at most 4096 characters long; a longer component is rejected with RuntimeError. Mutually exclusive with prim_paths.

  • prim_paths – Explicit list of physics-object paths. Mutually exclusive with pattern.

  • tensor_type – Tensor type enum value (TensorType.*).

  • raise_if_empty – If True, raise ValueError when the binding matches zero physics objects. The default keeps empty bindings valid. Prefer it for optional or broad queries and check binding.count.

Returns:

TensorBinding object for reading/writing tensor data.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If neither pattern nor prim_paths is provided, both are, or raise_if_empty is true and no physics objects match.

  • RuntimeError – If binding creation fails.

Examples:

import numpy as np
from ovphysx import TensorType

def use_tensor_bindings(physx):
    # Optional broad queries can be empty.
    with physx.create_tensor_binding(
        "/World/robot*", tensor_type=TensorType.RIGID_BODY_POSE
    ) as binding:
        if binding.count:
            poses = np.zeros(
                binding.shape, dtype=np.dtype(str(binding.dtype))
            )
            binding.read(poses)

    binding = physx.create_tensor_binding(
        prim_paths=["/World/env1/robot", "/World/env2/robot"],
        tensor_type=TensorType.ARTICULATION_DOF_POSITION_TARGET,
    )
    targets = np.zeros(
        binding.shape, dtype=np.dtype(str(binding.dtype))
    )
    binding.write(targets)
    binding.destroy()
Preconditions:

  • Exactly one of pattern or prim_paths must be provided.

  • A USD stage is loaded.

Side effects:

  • Allocates native binding resources.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • Returned TensorBinding retains native resources until destroy(). Each call returns an independent handle; destroying one binding does not invalidate a sibling selecting the same objects.

  • A new binding selects the currently eligible realized objects, even while an older binding for the same pattern remains alive.

  • Use binding.shape and binding.dtype (or binding.spec) for layout and binding.native_device for no-staging placement. Most tensor types are float32, but some types such as RIGID_BODY_DISABLE_SIMULATION are not.

  • The binding is tied to the current stage topology. Reuse it across steps, but do not keep it across detach_ovstage(), removing USD data that contains bound objects, or replacing/reparsing the stage so bound objects are destroyed and recreated. Destroy cached bindings before those lifecycle operations when practical. If a stale binding survives, only destroy it. Create replacements after the operation completes.

Diagnostics:

  • Pattern bindings can intentionally match zero physics objects, so expected TensorAPI no-match diagnostics are quieted on the simulation view used to create that binding.

  • Explicit prim_paths keep the default error-level no-match diagnostics for typo detection. To detect partial misses programmatically, compare the requested prim_paths with the resolved binding.prim_paths returned after creation.

Threading:

  • Do not create bindings concurrently with stage mutation.

Errors:

  • Raises ValueError for invalid arguments.

  • Raises RuntimeError on creation failure.

destroy() → None#

Destroy this PhysX instance.

Preconditions:

  • No other thread is using this instance. Calling destroy() again after terminal destruction is a valid no-op.

Side effects:

  • Releases native resources and unregisters the instance.

  • Collects all outstanding raw tasks and session operations, including step and clone receipts. They cannot be collected again afterward.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • All tensor bindings and contact bindings created by this instance are automatically released.

  • Object-change subscriptions and their Python callback captures are released after native subscription cleanup.

  • Drop every output-read Warp array and downstream view before destruction. Live aliases cause RuntimeError before teardown; the instance and arrays stay valid so destruction can be retried after dropping the aliases.

  • The instance becomes unusable after destruction.

Threading:

  • Do not call concurrently with other operations on this instance.

Errors:

  • Reports collected task and cleanup failures after attempting teardown; a TaskError can therefore be raised after the instance is destroyed.

  • Raises RuntimeError without changing the instance if called from a native log callback. Retry after the callback returns.

  • Raises RuntimeError and preserves ownership when native destruction returns INVALID_STATE because companion leases or a runtime/recording transition remain active. Close leases or finish the transition, then retry.

  • Other native destruction failures or process shutdown failures raise RuntimeError after terminal destruction; a later call is a no-op. If both fail, the process-shutdown error is reported with the native status included.

  • A Python or ctypes exception raised while invoking native destruction leaves ownership intact so the call can be retried.

  • Because this is a checked operation, a cleanup failure raised from a finally block becomes the active exception. Python preserves any in-flight exception as chained context; applications that need different precedence must catch and log cleanup failures explicitly.

detach_ovstage() → Task#

Submit Stage teardown and return its Task receipt.

Execution currently runs inline. Earlier tasks complete before teardown, but their outcomes remain uncollected. Collect this Task with wait_task(), or use wait_all() to collect every pending outcome. Wait for successful teardown before destroying the Stage. Detaching an unattached instance succeeds as a no-op task. Detach does not restore initial poses or reset simulation time. Clears registered interests and output-buffer registrations, so a subsequent attach_ovstage() to a different Stage starts clean. After detach, stage-dependent calls such as update_from_ovstage() and step() fail until a Stage is attached again. Detach invalidates the stage’s tensor, contact, and SDF views. Do not read, write, or evaluate existing bindings or SDF views. Destroy them and create replacements after calling attach_ovstage() and realizing a stage again. If this instance owns an active OVD recording, detach stops and finalizes it. Reattach stays dormant until an explicit recording start, which may occur before the next simulation step.

Errors:

  • Raises RuntimeError if submission or Python cleanup is rejected.

  • Accepted execution failures raise TaskError when collected. Teardown may partially retire resources on failure. The Stage remains retained while native ownership remains attached.

evaluate_sdf_shapes(
points,
out,
*,
prim_paths: list[int] | None = None,
pattern: str | None = None,
cuda_stream: int = 0,
cuda_wait_event: int = 0,
) → None#

Evaluate the signed distance fields of SDF collision shapes at the given points.

The successor of create_sdf_view() and SdfView.evaluate(). The shapes are the members of an SDF_SHAPE output query: the collision shapes the SDF view accepts, a collider carrying PhysxSDFMeshCollisionAPI whose shape is a triangle mesh with an SDF, runtime clones included. Rows follow the selection: prim_paths in the order given, pattern in the same match order as create_sdf_view(); with neither, every SDF shape, in the order the runtime stores them. A selected prim that is not an SDF shape is skipped, as the SDF view skipped it.

For each row i and point j, out[i, j] receives the gradient (x, y, z) and then the signed distance at points[i, j], negative inside. Points and gradients are in each shape’s mesh-local space (the unscaled frame of the mesh’s vertices); no transform is applied. Q, the points per shape, is read from the arrays on every call. A point outside the shape’s SDF grid (the mesh bounds padded by the SDF margin) is evaluated, not refused, as by the SDF view: its distance is the SDF value at the nearest grid point plus the distance to the grid, a positive upper bound, and its gradient points away from the shape. This waits for the evaluation, so out is complete when it returns.

Requires a GPU instance (DirectGPU). The first evaluation after loading USD may perform the automatic DirectGPU warmup step, as the SDF view did. After that it never steps: the scene must have simulated since physics objects were last created or released, as PhysX uploads shape data to the GPU only when it simulates, so step once after such a change.

Parameters:

  • points – DLPack-compatible float32 array of shape [N, Q, 3] on the CUDA device, N the number of selected SDF shapes.

  • out – Pre-allocated DLPack-compatible float32 array of shape [N, Q, 4] on the same device.

  • prim_paths – Optional native ovx_primpath_t handles naming the shapes, from the attached Stage’s path dictionary as for query(). Takes precedence over pattern.

  • pattern – Optional absolute path pattern naming the shapes, matched as in query(); the complete rules are on the “Path patterns” page of the ovphysx documentation.

  • cuda_stream – Producer stream of points still writing them, drained before they are read, as for WriteSession.commit(). Warp arrays and CUDA DLPack producers are synchronized already. Stream 1 names the legacy default stream of the current CUDA context.

  • cuda_wait_event – Producer completion event of points, waited on before they are read. out must have no outstanding device reads or writes when the call is made, unless that work is on cuda_stream or before cuda_wait_event; nothing else may use out until it returns.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If pattern is empty, or an array is not C-contiguous.

  • RuntimeError – If an array has the wrong dtype, shape or device, N is not the number of selected SDF shapes (the message states it) or exceeds 65535, N x Q exceeds 2^31 - 1, the instance is not DirectGPU, the scene has not simulated since physics objects last changed, the producer handoff fails, or the evaluation fails.

Submit a reusable selector. Handles and metadata require successful completion.

Explicit prim handles take precedence over a pattern. Selections use ALL scope and keep their resolved membership; a whole-type ACTIVE selector is reevaluated when a session opens. Metadata is a creation-time snapshot; use metadata=False to omit optional discovery work. contacts selects CONTACT_SENSOR rows and optional paired filters through ContactSelection; it cannot be combined with prim_paths, pattern, or ACTIVE scope. DEBUG_RENDER is this instance’s target: it needs no attached stage, and prim_paths, pattern, and contacts do not apply. Its scope is validated and then ignored.

attributes,

Submit a read-session open using a completed Query, without fetching.

Attributes are names or tokens from the owning Stage dictionary. Optional metadata describes availability at open; None never causes a later fetch. Use session.fetch_next().wait() to materialize a group on the current Warp stream. Native host completion does not synchronize unrelated CUDA streams.

Availability is per attribute and scene. Simulated DirectGPU columns need the first simulation step. isSleeping is a CPU uint8 snapshot (1 asleep, 0 awake); links report their articulation’s state. DirectGPU disables sleeping, so emitted values are 0 and its existing step-first and disabled body omission rules apply. Use an ALL-scope query to include sleeping bodies on modes that support sleep.

value: bool | int | float | str,
) → None#

Set one value retained by this instance.

static set_cpu_mode(cpu_only: bool) → None#

Compatibility wrapper for GlobalConfigKey.CPU_ONLY.

Call before the first PhysX instance is ever created to keep ovphysx’s own code from touching CUDA. The call requires no active instances. Once set to True successfully, the mode cannot be reversed for this process.

When called before the first instance, True prevents CUDA driver use by ovphysx and makes all PhysX scenes use CPU dynamics regardless of their USD physxScene:enableGPUDynamics settings. Other libraries in the process may still open the driver. A call after an earlier instance was destroyed may succeed, but cannot provide ovphysx’s no-CUDA-touch guarantee or retarget an already-bootstrapped runtime. For CPU-only deployments, setting OVPHYSX_DISABLE_GPU before ovphysx initialization provides the equivalent process-wide policy.

Raises:

RuntimeError – If any PhysX instances are currently active, or if attempting to set False after True has been applied (CPU-only mode is sticky as soon as enabling it succeeds).

start_recording(destination: OmniPvdDestination) → None#

Start an explicit OVD recording session.

Make the shared runtime OVD recording capable before the first PhysX() by calling set_global_config(GlobalConfigKey.OVD_RECORDING_CAPABLE, True). The key defaults to false; capability alone does not start output. Attach a physics stage before calling this method; recording may start before the first simulation step. Creation and attachment stay dormant. Any PhysX instance sharing a capable runtime may start a session while none is active; that instance then owns it. A runtime created without capability rejects start with INVALID_STATE and an error naming the capability key. Unsupported platforms retain NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

A failed validation or destination-open attempt may be retried. A start while recording is active is invalid and does not replace its destination. After stop, another FILE or TCP session may be started.

step(dt: float) → Task#

Initiate a physics step and return its Task receipt.

Simulation time is tracked internally. Each step advances it by dt. The timestep is passed through without clamping or substepping; choose a timestep appropriate for the simulation.

A dt of 0.0 is accepted but simulates nothing: it advances no simulation time and leaves all state, including the contacts and timestep that contact reads use, exactly as the previous step left them.

Parameters:

dt – Finite, nonnegative delta time in seconds.

Returns:

Immutable Task receipt for use with wait_task().

Example:

def step_and_collect(physx):
    task = physx.step(0.016)
    physx.wait_task(task)
Preconditions:

  • An ovstage Stage is attached to this instance.

Side effects:

  • Advances simulation time and mutates physics state.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • The receipt owns no simulation resources. A terminal outcome is collected once by wait_task() or wait_all().

Threading:

  • Do not call concurrently on the same instance without external sync.

Errors:

  • Raises RuntimeError on failure to enqueue.

  • Accepted execution failures raise TaskError when collected by a wait.

step_sync(dt: float) → None#

Step simulation and wait for completion in a single call.

Faster than step() + wait_task() for performance-critical applications like RL training that always wait immediately. Simulation time is tracked internally and advanced by dt.

A dt of 0.0 simulates nothing, exactly as in step().

Parameters:

dt – Finite, nonnegative delta time [s], passed through as in step().

Raises:

RuntimeError – If the step or wait fails.

stop_recording() → None#

Stop and finalize the OVD recording owned by this instance.

Peer instances cannot stop another owner’s session.

update_articulations_kinematic(
*,
flags: ArticulationKinematicFlag = ArticulationKinematicFlag.POSITION | ArticulationKinematicFlag.VELOCITY,
scope: ObjectScope = ObjectScope.ALL,
prim_paths: list[int] | None = None,
pattern: str | None = None,
) → None#

Update selected articulation link state from current generalized state.

The articulations updated are the members of an ARTICULATION output query: every articulation in scope, or only those a prim_paths / pattern selection names, with the same selection rules as query(). Articulations outside the selection are left unchanged. This waits for the query and forward-kinematics tasks and raises any execution failure. It returns None after updating link poses and/or velocities without running a normal simulation step, collision detection, or contact generation.

In GPU mode, the first kinematic update after loading USD may perform the same automatic DirectGPU warmup step used by tensor reads/writes.

Parameters:

  • flags – POSITION, VELOCITY, or both. Zero validates the query and does no update.

  • scope – ALL articulations or the current ACTIVE articulation set. A selection has no scope, so combining prim_paths or pattern with ACTIVE raises ValueError.

  • prim_paths – Optional native ovx_primpath_t handles naming the articulations to update, from the attached Stage’s path dictionary as for query(). A handle of an articulation’s link or joint selects that articulation. Takes precedence over pattern.

  • pattern – Optional absolute path pattern naming the articulations to update, matched as in query(); the complete rules are on the “Path patterns” page of the ovphysx documentation.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If a selection is combined with scope=ACTIVE, or pattern is empty.

  • RuntimeError – If the update fails.

update_from_ovstage(
from_ordinal: int,
to_ordinal: int,
) → Task#

Submit committed edits over [from_ordinal, to_ordinal] and return a Task.

The application that writes to ovstage owns the ordinal range and calls this after sealing the writes. population.apply_usd_changes() waits for population work but does not seal its ordinal; complete stage.advance_write_floor(ordinal).wait() before this call. ovphysx forwards the range (as ovstage’s own ovstage_ordinal_range_t) to the runtime ovstage change feed and applies the resulting deltas to the simulation.

Ordinals at or below the latest successfully consumed ordinal are skipped. A fully consumed range succeeds as a no-op. An overlapping range applies only its unread suffix. attach_ovstage() consumes its initial read_ordinal, so replaying it does not repeat initial population events. Later authored and sealed population changes are applied normally.

Execution currently runs inline. Collect the Task with wait_task() or wait_all() to observe execution failure before relying on the updated state. Submission errors raise RuntimeError immediately; accepted execution failures raise TaskError at collection. Keep the sealed data readable until completion.

wait_all(*, timeout_ns: int | None = None) → None#

Collect uncollected tasks accepted before this call began.

Tasks are collected in submission order with one readiness deadline. Completed successes and failures are collected once. A timeout stops at the earliest unfinished task, leaving it and later tasks uncollected. Failures remain reportable even when their original receipts were discarded.

Parameters:

timeout_ns – Readiness timeout in nanoseconds, with the same semantics as wait_task(). None waits indefinitely; 0 polls once.

Returns:

None on success, including an empty or already-collected task set.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If timeout_ns is outside 0 through 2**64 - 1.

  • TaskError – If collected tasks failed. The errors property contains immutable (Task, message) entries with copied text.

  • TaskTimeoutError – If work remains unfinished at the deadline, even when earlier tasks failed. The errors property contains those earlier failures; pending_task identifies the earliest unfinished task. Collected failures are not repeated by later waits.

  • RuntimeError – If the instance is invalid or the wait itself fails.

Serialize calls on each instance externally.

wait_task(
task: Task,
*,
timeout_ns: int | None = None,
) → None#

Wait for and collect only the supplied task’s terminal outcome.

Parameters:

  • task – Task receipt returned by this instance.

  • timeout_ns – Readiness timeout in nanoseconds. None waits indefinitely; 0 polls once. Finalization after readiness can exceed the timeout.

Returns:

None on success.

Raises:

  • TypeError – If task is not a Task.

  • ValueError – If timeout_ns is outside 0 through 2**64 - 1.

  • TaskError – If this task failed. The exception owns copied error text.

  • TaskTimeoutError – If the task is unfinished at the deadline. Its pending_task remains available for another wait.

  • RuntimeError – If the instance or receipt is invalid, the task was already collected, or the wait itself fails.

Waiting for B never reports or collects A’s failure. A completed outcome can be collected once; internal synchronization does not collect it. Serialize calls on each instance externally.

Example:

from ovphysx import TaskTimeoutError

def poll_task(physx, task):
    try:
        physx.wait_task(task, timeout_ns=0)
    except TaskTimeoutError:
        return False
    return True
warmup() → None#

Explicitly run the warmup step (synchronous).

On first call, runs a minimal simulation step (~1ns) to initialize PhysX structures. Works in both CPU and GPU mode (in GPU mode this also populates DirectGPU buffers).

Normally done automatically on the first tensor read, but calling it explicitly lets you control when the latency occurs.

This function is idempotent. Calling it multiple times has no effect after the first successful call. Warmup state resets after detach_ovstage() or attaching a new USD stage.

Raises:

RuntimeError – If warmup fails.

Side effects:

  • Advances simulation by a minimal timestep on first call.

Threading:

  • Do not call concurrently with other operations on this instance.

Open validates every requested writable attribute before exposing groups. It publishes no values. Fetch indices refer to the original request order; each commit has its own task and may fail after earlier commits applied.

class ovphysx.api.TensorBinding(
sdk,
handle: int,
tensor_type: int,
ndim: int,
shape: tuple,
dtype: DLDataType | None = None,
*,
_from_factory: bool = False,
)#

Bases: object

Tensor binding for bulk physics data access via DLPack.

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The tensor-binding API is deprecated. Use PhysX.read() for reads and PhysX.write() for writes.

A tensor binding connects a physics-object path pattern to a tensor type, enabling efficient bulk read/write for authored USD objects and runtime-only clones (poses, velocities, joint positions, etc.). The shape, ndim, and dtype metadata come from ovphysx_get_tensor_binding_spec(). Use them to allocate compatible buffers instead of assuming every tensor type is float32. Use native_device to choose the no-staging CPU or CUDA device.

CPU-only property bindings cover standalone rigid-body mass/inertia/COM values, articulation DOF/body properties, rigid-body/articulation shape properties, deformable-material properties, and disable-simulation/gravity flags. Fixed and spatial tendon property bindings are not CPU-only. CPU-only property bindings require host-resident tensor, index, and mask buffers, including when the simulation runs on GPU.

This is a synchronous API - operations complete before returning. Bindings are tied to the currently realized physics objects. Reuse them across simulation steps, but do not keep them across detach_ovstage(), removing USD data that contains bound objects, or replacing/reparsing the stage so bound objects are destroyed and recreated. Destroy cached bindings before those lifecycle operations when practical. If a stale binding survives, only destroy it. Create replacement bindings after the operation completes.

Usage patterns:

  • Context manager (auto-cleanup):

    import numpy as np
from ovphysx import TensorType

def raise_robot_poses(physx):
    with physx.create_tensor_binding(
        "/World/robot*", tensor_type=TensorType.RIGID_BODY_POSE
    ) as binding:
        poses = np.zeros(binding.shape, dtype=np.dtype(str(binding.dtype)))
        binding.read(poses)
        poses[:, 2] += 0.1  # raise z position
        binding.write(poses)
    # Auto-destroyed here

  • Manual (explicit cleanup):

    import numpy as np
from ovphysx import TensorType

def read_robot_poses(physx):
    binding = physx.create_tensor_binding(
        "/World/robot*", tensor_type=TensorType.RIGID_BODY_POSE
    )
    poses = np.zeros(binding.shape, dtype=np.dtype(str(binding.dtype)))
    binding.read(poses)
    binding.destroy()
    return poses
property body_count: int#

Number of links.

property body_names: list[str]#

List of body/link names.

property count: int#

Get number of entities (first dimension of shape).

destroy() → None#

Release binding resources.

Safe to call multiple times. Called automatically on garbage collection or when exiting a context manager.

Preconditions:

  • Binding must not be in use by other threads.

Side effects:

  • Releases native resources and invalidates the binding.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • After destruction, the binding cannot be used.

Threading:

  • Serialized per binding via an internal lock.

Errors:

  • RuntimeError if destruction fails.

property dof_count: int#

Number of degrees of freedom (DOFs). 0 if not an articulation binding.

property dof_names: list[str]#

List of DOF names (one per DOF).

property dtype: DLDataType#

Get the required DLPack dtype for tensors passed to this binding.

Most bindings use float32. Index bindings (deformable element indices) use int32. The bool bindings (DISABLE_SIMULATION, DISABLE_GRAVITY) use uint8, as does ARTICULATION_DOF_DRIVE_TYPE, which is a per-DOF enum byte rather than a flag. See dtype_name for a compact string form.

property dtype_name: str#

Get the required tensor dtype as a short string such as float32, int32, or uint8.

property fixed_tendon_count: int#

Number of fixed tendons per articulation (0 if none).

Use to decide whether to allocate buffers for fixed tendon property tensors (types 80-85) and to skip tendon code paths when T=0.

property handle: int#

Get the binding handle.

property is_fixed_base: bool#

Whether the articulation has a fixed base.

property joint_count: int#

Number of joints per articulation.

property joint_names: list[str]#

List of joint names.

property native_device: DLDevice#

Get the binding’s native DLPack device.

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The tensor-binding API is deprecated. Use PhysX.read() for reads and PhysX.write() for writes.

CPU-only property tensors report DLDevice(kDLCPU, 0) even when the scene uses GPU dynamics. Other bindings follow their native TensorAPI view and report DLDevice(kDLCUDA, ordinal) in DirectGPU mode or DLDevice(kDLCPU, 0) otherwise. This property identifies the no-staging device and does not change existing read/write behavior. A CUDA device_id is the process-visible runtime ordinal used by a framework device such as cuda:N, not a physical PCI bus index. Compare device_type.value with a constant such as DLDeviceType.kDLCUDA. This is a live query, not cached metadata: it may wait for pending operations and rejects an invalidated simulation view.

property ndim: int#

Get the number of dimensions reported by ovphysx_get_tensor_binding_spec().

property prim_paths: list[str]#

Resolved physics-object paths in tensor row order.

Rigid-body bindings return one path per rigid-body tensor row. Articulation bindings return one root object path per articulation row. For per-articulation link names, use body_names.

read(tensor) → None#

Read simulation data into a user-provided tensor (synchronous).

The tensor must have matching shape and dtype (shape and dtype). Can be a NumPy array, PyTorch tensor, or any object with __dlpack__ protocol.

When called repeatedly with the same NumPy, PyTorch, Warp, or direct DLTensor buffer object, an internal cache reuses descriptor metadata and attribute lookups. CUDA DLPack producers still export a capsule on each call to establish stream readiness. The numpy writeable guard is preserved on the fast path. Other DLPack providers are reacquired on every call. Callers that want the fast path should reuse the same tensor object with unchanged backing storage across calls. Do not resize or rebind storage between cached calls. The staleness guard rebuilds the cache when it detects a pointer change, but storage mutations that reuse the same pointer violate the cache contract. Direct DLTensor inputs retain their caller-owned descriptor.

Parameters:

tensor – DLPack-compatible tensor with pre-allocated storage matching self.shape. Must use self.dtype. When CUDA is available, CPU/CUDA device mismatches are staged for binding types whose storage follows the simulation device. CPU-only property bindings require a host-resident tensor (kDLCPU or kDLCUDAHost), including on GPU simulations; CUDA and CUDA-managed tensors are rejected rather than staged. Cross-GPU mismatches and CUDA tensors in process-wide CPU-only mode are rejected.

Preconditions:

  • This binding is not destroyed.

  • tensor has matching shape and dtype and uses a supported device.

  • Raw DLTensor buffers must be ready for native access; callers must finish pending CUDA work on them before the call. Objects implementing the CUDA DLPack stream protocol are synchronized through Warp.

Side effects:

  • Blocks until data is available and writes into the provided tensor.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • Caller owns tensor storage and must keep it alive for the duration of the call.

  • Do not mutate the tensor’s backing storage (resize(), set_(), etc.) between cached calls. A staleness guard detects pointer changes for NumPy, PyTorch, and Warp inputs and falls back to the slow path. Direct DLTensor inputs retain their caller-owned descriptor.

Threading:

  • Serialized per binding via an internal lock.

Errors:

  • RuntimeError if read fails (shape mismatch, device mismatch, etc.).

property shape: tuple#

Get tensor shape as tuple reported by ovphysx_get_tensor_binding_spec().

Returns:

Tensor dimensions for this binding. Scalar-property bindings use (N,). Flat state tensors use (N, C). Articulation and deformable mesh tensors use (N, L, C).

sleep(indices=None) → None#

Force rigid bodies in this binding to sleep.

Mirrors PhysX SDK PxRigidDynamic::putToSleep. Symmetric counterpart to wake_up(). Bodies that have RIGID_BODY_DISABLE_SIMULATION set are silently skipped.

Only valid on a rigid-body binding. Articulation bindings raise.

Parameters:

indices – Optional int32 DLPack-compatible tensor of indices into this binding. If None, every body in the binding is put to sleep.

Errors:

RuntimeError if the binding is destroyed, is not a rigid-body binding, has been invalidated by a stage change, or the engine call fails.

property spatial_tendon_count: int#

Number of spatial tendons per articulation (0 if none).

Use to decide whether to allocate buffers for spatial tendon property tensors (types 90-93) and to skip tendon code paths when T=0.

property spec: TensorBindingSpec#

Get a Python-owned tensor spec snapshot for this binding.

property tensor_type: int#

Get the tensor type enum value.

wake_up(indices=None) → None#

Wake rigid bodies in this binding.

Mirrors PhysX SDK PxRigidDynamic::wakeUp. Bodies that still have RIGID_BODY_DISABLE_SIMULATION set are silently skipped (the engine refuses to wake disabled actors).

Typical pair: clear the disable flag on an actor (re-add it to simulation in a sleep state) and then call this so the actor is active for the next step().

Only valid on a rigid-body binding. Articulation bindings raise.

Parameters:

indices – Optional int32 DLPack-compatible tensor of indices into this binding. If None, every body in the binding is woken.

Errors:

RuntimeError if the binding is destroyed, is not a rigid-body binding, has been invalidated by a stage change, or the engine wake call fails.

write(tensor, indices=None, mask=None) → None#

Write data from a user-provided tensor into the simulation (synchronous).

The tensor must have matching shape and dtype (shape and dtype). Can be a NumPy array, PyTorch tensor, or any object with __dlpack__ protocol.

When called repeatedly with the same supported buffer object and no indices/mask, an internal cache reuses descriptor metadata and attribute lookups. Producer readiness is checked on every call. Callers that want this fast path should reuse the same tensor object with unchanged backing storage across calls. See read() for the supported providers and full contract.

Parameters:

  • tensor – DLPack-compatible tensor with data to write, shape matching self.shape. Must use self.dtype. When CUDA is available, CPU/CUDA device mismatches are staged for binding types whose storage follows the simulation device. For CPU-only property bindings, this tensor and optional indices or mask must be host-resident (kDLCPU or kDLCUDAHost), including on GPU simulations; CUDA and CUDA-managed tensors are rejected rather than staged. Cross-GPU mismatches and CUDA tensors in process-wide CPU-only mode are rejected.

  • indices – Optional int32 tensor of indices for partial update. If provided, only the rows at the given indices are written. The tensor argument must still be full shape [N, …] matching the binding spec; only the selected rows are applied. Shape of indices: [K] where K <= N.

  • mask –

    Optional bool/uint8 tensor for masked update. If provided, only elements where mask[i] != 0 are written. Shape: [N] matching the binding’s first dimension. When mask is provided, tensor must be full shape [N, …]. If both mask and indices are provided, mask takes precedence and indices are ignored (with a warning).

    Note: there is no corresponding read(..., mask=...). Reads always return the full [N,…] tensor and callers can index the result themselves. This write-only mask design matches other RL physics APIs such as Newton’s selectionAPI, where masks selectively apply actions but observations are always returned in full.

Preconditions:

  • This binding is not destroyed.

  • tensor matches shape and dtype and uses a supported device.

  • indices (if provided) is int32 and within bounds.

  • mask (if provided) is bool/uint8 with shape [N] on a supported device.

Side effects:

  • Updates simulation state for the bound entities.

Ownership/Lifetime:

  • Caller owns tensor/indices/mask storage and must keep it alive for the call.

Threading:

  • Serialized per binding via an internal lock.

Errors:

  • RuntimeError if write fails (shape mismatch, device mismatch, etc.).

Do not instantiate directly. Use PhysX.create_contact_binding() to obtain an instance. The sensor_paths and filter_paths properties expose the row/column metadata for the returned tensors.

destroy() → None#

Release contact binding resources.

Safe to call multiple times. Captures strong references to the SDK and library before the C call to guard against GC ordering issues (Python may collect self._sdk before self if both go out of scope together).

property filter_count: int#

Number of filter bodies per sensor (0 when no filters specified).

property filter_paths: list[list[str]]#

Resolved filter physics-object paths in contact tensor column order.

The outer list is indexed by sensor row and the inner list by filter column. Each inner list is empty for unfiltered contact bindings (i.e. when filter_count == 0).

Returns:

Nested list of shape [sensor_count][filter_count].

Return type:

list[list[str]]

get_other_actor_paths_from_ids(ids_array) → list[str]#

Resolve actor IDs from read_raw_contact_data() to physics-object paths.

ids_array is a 1D int64/uint64 array (numpy / warp / torch with DLPack support) holding actor IDs, from either column of the actor_ids tensor. Both use the same namespace. A column is a strided view and this boundary requires C-contiguous input, so wrap a column slice in np.ascontiguousarray() before passing it. Path strings are copied into Python, so the caller can keep them across subsequent ovphysx calls.

Every non-zero ID is checked against the attached stage first, so an ID whose actor has been removed yields an empty path rather than the path it used to name. Since the caller holds the IDs, that makes the failure explicit: a non-zero ID with an empty path is stale, while ID 0 simply means no actor. The check is as precise as the backend’s notion of existence. On a USD stage a merely deactivated prim still resolves.

Returns:

Physics-object paths in the same order as the input IDs.

Return type:

list[str]

property max_contact_data_count: int#

Flat-buffer capacity for detailed contact and friction reads.

read_contact_data(
contact_forces,
positions,
normals,
separations,
counts,
start_indices,
) → int#

Deprecated alias of read_normal_contact_data(); forces contain only normal components.

read_force_matrix(output) → None#

Deprecated alias of read_normal_force_matrix(); returns normal forces only.

read_friction_contact_data(
friction_forces,
friction_points,
counts,
start_indices,
) → int#

Read detailed friction contact data into flat buffers.

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The contact-binding API is deprecated and retained for compatibility.

Returns world-space friction force vectors at friction anchors. These anchors need not correspond one-to-one with the contact points from read_normal_contact_data(); use this read’s own counts and start indices.

Expected shapes are [C, 3] for friction_forces and friction_points, and [sensor_count, filter_count] for counts and start_indices. C is max_contact_data_count and must be positive, and filter_count must also be positive. Count and start-index tensors may be int32 or uint32. Friction entries are per-anchor. Sum each flat slice to build a pair-level [sensor_count, filter_count, 3] force tensor. Friction forces use the timestep from the last successful PhysX.step() or PhysX.step_sync() call that simulated; a zero-dt step is skipped and changes neither the contacts nor the timestep.

Returns the total number of friction anchors produced for the step. When this exceeds max_contact_data_count, the buffers contain the valid prefix that fit. A pair’s count reports only anchors actually written, and its start index is clamped to max_contact_data_count, so [start, start + count) is always an in-range (possibly empty) slice. Recreate the binding with at least the returned capacity, step again, and retry to obtain a complete result.

read_friction_data(
friction_forces,
friction_points,
counts,
start_indices,
) → int#

Deprecated alias of read_friction_contact_data().

read_friction_force_matrix(output) → None#

Read friction forces into output, shape [sensor_count, filter_count, 3].

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The contact-binding API is deprecated and retained for compatibility.

Each entry sums world-space friction forces for its sensor/filter pair, independently of detailed-contact capacity. Only contacts with configured filter bodies contribute. Adding read_normal_force_matrix() from the same step yields total contact forces for those pairs. Individual friction forces and anchor points are available through read_friction_contact_data().

Impulse-to-force conversion uses the dt of the last step that actually simulated; a zero-dt step is skipped and changes neither the contacts nor the dt.

read_net_forces(output) → None#

Deprecated alias of read_net_normal_forces(); returns normal forces only.

read_net_friction_forces(output) → None#

Read net friction forces into output, shape [sensor_count, 3].

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The contact-binding API is deprecated and retained for compatibility.

Sums world-space friction-anchor forces over all reported contacts of each sensor, including contacts with bodies not matched by the configured filters. Filters and detailed-contact capacity are not required. Adding the result to read_net_normal_forces() from the same step yields the total contact force. Impulse-to-force conversion uses that step’s dt.

For example, if a foot touches the floor and a wall but its filter selects only the floor, this function includes friction from both bodies. The friction force matrix includes only the floor contribution.

Opposing anchor forces may cancel while producing torque. This vector sum does not report friction torque.

read_net_normal_forces(output) → None#

Read net normal forces into output, shape [sensor_count, 3].

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The contact-binding API is deprecated and retained for compatibility.

Sums world-space normal forces over all reported contacts of each sensor, regardless of filters or detailed-contact capacity. Add read_net_friction_forces() from the same step for total contact force. Impulse-to-force conversion uses the dt of the last step that actually simulated; a zero-dt step is skipped and changes neither the contacts nor the dt.

read_normal_contact_data(
contact_forces,
positions,
normals,
separations,
counts,
start_indices,
) → int#

Read detailed normal contact data into flat buffers.

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The contact-binding API is deprecated and retained for compatibility.

contact_forces contains scalar normal forces. Multiply each scalar by the corresponding normals vector to obtain the world-space normal force vector. Friction forces are returned separately by read_friction_contact_data().

Expected shapes are [C, 1] for contact_forces and separations, [C, 3] for positions and normals, and [sensor_count, filter_count] for counts and start_indices. C is max_contact_data_count. Both C and filter_count must be positive. Count and start-index tensors may be int32 or uint32. Contact force magnitudes use the timestep from the last successful PhysX.step() or PhysX.step_sync() call that simulated; a zero-dt step is skipped and changes neither the contacts nor the timestep.

Returns the total number of contacts produced for the step. When this exceeds max_contact_data_count, the buffers contain the valid prefix that fit. A pair’s count reports only contacts actually written, and its start index is clamped to max_contact_data_count, so [start, start + count) is always an in-range (possibly empty) slice. Recreate the binding with at least the returned capacity, step again, and retry to obtain a complete result.

read_normal_force_matrix(output) → None#

Read normal forces into output, shape [sensor_count, filter_count, 3].

Deprecated since version 0.6.0: The contact-binding API is deprecated and retained for compatibility.

Each entry sums world-space normal forces for its sensor/filter pair, independently of detailed-contact capacity. Adding read_friction_force_matrix() from the same step yields total contact forces for the configured pairs. Impulse-to-force conversion uses the dt of the last step that actually simulated; a zero-dt step is skipped and changes neither the contacts nor the dt.

read_raw_contact_data(
contact_forces,
positions,
normals,
separations,
sensor_layout,
actor_ids,
) → int#

Read raw (unfiltered) contact data into flat buffers.

Filter-less variant of read_normal_contact_data(). Returns every contact involving each sensor regardless of which other actor it collided with, plus per-contact actor-identity tensors for identifying both the sensor and the contacting body via get_other_actor_paths_from_ids().

Expected shapes are [C, 1] for contact_forces and separations, [C, 3] for positions and normals, [sensor_count, 2] for sensor_layout (column 0 count, column 1 start index), and [C, 2] for actor_ids (column 0 the reporting sensor’s actor, column 1 the actor it contacted). C is max_contact_data_count and must be positive. No filter dimension is required. sensor_layout may be int32 or uint32. actor_ids must be int64 or uint64. Slicing the columns out as views costs no copy. Contact force magnitudes use the timestep from the last successful PhysX.step() or PhysX.step_sync() call that simulated; a zero-dt step is skipped and changes neither the contacts nor the timestep.

Returns the total number of contacts produced for the step. When this exceeds max_contact_data_count, the buffers contain the valid prefix that fit. A sensor’s count reports only contacts actually written, and its start index is clamped to max_contact_data_count, so [start, start + count) is always an in-range (possibly empty) slice. Recreate the binding with at least the returned capacity, step again, and retry to obtain a complete result.

Token lifetime: tokens in actor_ids are opaque actor handles, not encoded paths, and are stable while the corresponding actor is alive on the attached stage. After an actor is removed, its token is stale and get_other_actor_paths_from_ids() reports it as an empty path rather than as the path it used to name.

Number of sensor bodies matched.

property sensor_paths: list[str]#

Resolved sensor physics-object paths in contact tensor row order.

Returns:

One path per sensor row, in the same order as the contact data tensors.

Return type:

list[str]

Task Completion#

PhysX.step(), PhysX.clone(), PhysX.attach_ovstage(), PhysX.update_from_ovstage() and PhysX.detach_ovstage() return an immutable Task receipt. Collect one task’s outcome with ovphysx.api.PhysX.wait_task() or every uncollected task with ovphysx.api.PhysX.wait_all(); both return None on success and raise the exceptions below on failure or timeout.

Stage lifecycle tasks currently execute inline, but a returned receipt reports admission only. Keep the Stage alive until successful detach or instance destruction, and wait before consuming the result of attach or update. PhysX.is_stage_attached() is a synchronous ownership snapshot, not a completion or readiness check. PhysX.reset_stage() has been removed; use PhysX.detach_ovstage() for teardown. Neither operation restores initial poses.

The session API (query(), read(), write(), fetch_next(), commit() and close()) returns an Operation without waiting. Operation.wait() collects its native tasks and returns the typed result; Operation.result never waits. wait_all() also collects outstanding operations and caches their outcomes. read_sync(), read_tokens_sync(), write_sync(), commit_sync(), close_sync(), update_articulations_kinematic() and evaluate_sdf_shapes() wait for their native tasks internally. Waiting raises TaskError for accepted execution failures. ctypes exposes the complete native receipts. CUDA producer-event and consumer-stream dependencies remain necessary; a completed host task does not imply all GPU work is finished.

Run custom application code directly after the relevant task wait succeeds. wait_task(task) collects only that task; wait_all() also collects and acknowledges earlier uncollected outcomes, including failures.

class ovphysx.api.Task(status: ApiStatus, op_index: int, instance: int)#

Bases: object

Immutable receipt for an accepted operation, without instance ownership.

Pass the receipt to PhysX.wait_task on its owning instance. Completion is collected once, either by that wait or by PhysX.wait_all. Discarding a receipt does not discard an uncollected failure. status describes admission, op_index identifies the task within its instance, and instance is the owning native handle without a lifetime reference.

exception ovphysx.api.TaskError(errors: tuple[tuple[Task, str], ...])#

Bases: RuntimeError

Collected task failures, copied independently of native result storage.

property errors: tuple[tuple[Task, str], ...]#

Immutable (Task, message) entries in collection order.

exception ovphysx.api.TaskTimeoutError(
errors: tuple[tuple[Task, str], ...],
pending_task: Task,
)#

Bases: TimeoutError

A wait deadline expired, possibly after collecting earlier failures.

property errors: tuple[tuple[Task, str], ...]#

Immutable completed failures collected before the pending task.

property pending_task: Task#

Earliest unfinished task, which remains available for another wait.

Session Read/Write#

ovphysx.api.PhysX.query(), ovphysx.api.PhysX.read() and ovphysx.api.PhysX.write() return operations whose results are the types below. The Overview pages describe the data contract.

class ovphysx.api.Operation(
sdk,
tasks=(),
*,
convert=lambda : ...,
cleanup=None,
keepalive=(),
on_complete=None,
owners=(),
)#

A typed result of zero, one, or several real native tasks.

wait() collects completion explicitly. result never waits and raises while an outcome is uncollected. Outcomes are cached after either operation waits or the owning PhysX instance’s waits. Payload conversion runs once on first result access, on the submitting thread. In particular, read arrays use the Warp stream current at that access, not the stream used by wait_all.

Inputs and output slots survive until collection, even if the operation is dropped. Periodically call wait_all() for fire-and-forget submissions. Collecting Python-owned receipts directly through the C API is unsupported.

property done: bool#

Whether every native outcome has been collected; does not poll.

property result: T#

Return the cached typed result without waiting.

property task#

The native receipt, available only for a single-task operation.

property tasks#

Immutable tuple of the operation’s real native receipts.

wait(
*,
timeout_ns: int | None = None,
) → T#

Collect this operation’s tasks and return its typed result.

A finite timeout is one readiness budget across all constituent tasks. Completed failures are cached, including when a later task times out.

class ovphysx.api.Query(sdk, handle, object_type, metadata, stage, attachment)#

A completed reusable selector owned by one instance and attachment.

Release independently of sessions already opened from it. Whole-type queries evaluate membership at each session open; selected queries keep their resolved membership. Recreate a query to refresh its creation-time discovery metadata.

property dictionary#

Owner-aware PathDictionary for tokens and prim lists of this query.

class ovphysx.api.ReadResult(
sdk,
query: int,
read: int,
groups=None,
group_ids=(),
release=None,
*,
metadata=None,
object_type=SimObjectType.RIGID_BODY,
stage=None,
attachment=None,
)#

A completed read session with explicit asynchronous group fetches.

fetch_next().wait() exposes one group, or None at successful EOF. Opening a session does not fetch its groups. Numeric Warp aliases keep snapshot storage alive after logical close; dictionary metadata does not survive group release or attachment invalidation. The caller’s Query is independent.

close() → Operation[None]#

Logically close and submit group releases, without waiting for aliases.

The owner reference drops once every group release is admitted. Rejected admission retains it for retry. Pending fetches and returned arrays keep the physical snapshot alive until their own references are retired.

property dictionary#

Owner-aware dictionary; never resolves through a retired query.

fetch_next() → Operation[ReadGroup | None]#

Submit one fetch; materialize its arrays only on typed result access.

release() → Operation[None]#

Logically close and submit group releases, without waiting for aliases.

The owner reference drops once every group release is admitted. Rejected admission retains it for retry. Pending fetches and returned arrays keep the physical snapshot alive until their own references are retired.

class ovphysx.api.ReadGroup(
attribute: int,
object_type: SimObjectType,
ordinal: int,
is_array: bool,
is_delete: bool,
semantic: int,
prim_list: int,
prim_offset: int,
prim_count: int,
prim_index_map: object,
index_map: object,
layout_generation: int,
write_floor_ordinal: int,
tensors: list,
cuda_stream: int = 0,
cuda_wait_event: int = 0,
)#

One physics-output column group returned by ReadResult.fetch_next().

A flattened view of the native ovstage_read_group_t the read returns (its prims / data / meta sub-structs unpacked into these fields). The interned identifiers (attribute token and prim_list handle) resolve through the owning attached Stage path dictionary, so an ovstage.PathDictionary(stage) resolves them, and prim_list feeds straight into stage.query_from_path_list for a no-repack write-back. object_type is NOT part of the native group (the read is opened over one type). It is stamped here from the object_type of the session’s Query.

Constant on the physics-output path (so callers can rely on them): is_delete is always False (this read never emits tombstones). prim_offset is 0 and prim_index_map is None (each group carries its own full prim_list). ordinal is 0 (groups are not ordinal-stamped here).

attribute#

Interned EMITTED attribute token (resolve via the path dictionary). May differ from the requested name: a “position” request on a point-instancer is emitted as “positions” (instancer-local). Write back using this token, not the requested string.

Type:

int

object_type#

The queried SimObjectType (stamped from the query, not carried by the native ovstage group).

Type:

ovphysx.types.SimObjectType

ordinal#

The data ordinal of this group (0 on this path).

Type:

int

is_array#

Follows the SOURCE attribute kind: True for a ragged / USD-array / byte-string column (e.g. a point-instancer’s positions, a deformable mesh’s points), False for a fixed scalar column. It is NOT decided by whether the per-element dims happen to be uniform: a fixed-width array attribute is still is_array=True. It is the only signal that tells e.g. a 1-byte string from a scalar uint8 apart.

Type:

bool

is_delete#

Always False for physics output (tombstone flag).

Type:

bool

semantic#

Authored USD interpretation (ovstage_attribute_semantic_t value).

Type:

int

prim_list#

Interned prim-path-list handle covering this group’s prims.

Type:

int

prim_offset#

Start index within prim_list (0 on this path).

Type:

int

prim_count#

Number of prims in this group.

Type:

int

prim_index_map#

CPU warp.array of uint32 sparse indices into prim_list, or None for a contiguous range (always None on this path).

Type:

object

index_map#

CPU warp.array of uint32 values (gather/scatter over the OUTER element axis), or None. None for point-instancer rigid-body output, which always emits the instancer’s full instance array (by-index) so it forwards into the ovstage write path verbatim. Slots without a live body are zero-filled in every array; an all-zero orientations quaternion is the absent-slot marker because live orientations are normalized and never all zero.

Type:

object

layout_generation#

Reserved metadata field. The current output producer always returns 0. Do not use it for structural invalidation.

Type:

int

write_floor_ordinal#

Reserved metadata field. The current output producer always returns 0. The application owns ovstage write-floor advancement.

Type:

int

tensors#

One warp.array per native tensor (1 for a fixed column; per-prim for an array group). A tuple width above 1 is the trailing dim (a vec3 column is shape [N, 3]); a single-lane column stays [N]. Non-empty arrays alias the read session’s snapshot storage and keep it alive, so CPU and CUDA arrays are both safe to keep after the ReadResult closes.

Type:

list

cuda_stream#

Producer stream for a device column, or 0. The read emits 0: it does not ask a consumer to drain a stream, which is what a non-zero value means to ovstage.

Type:

int

cuda_wait_event#

CUDA event (as an integer handle) that a device column’s producer work signals, or 0 for a host column. A device column is handed over before its work has necessarily completed. The read does not block on the consumer’s behalf.

The Python binding enqueues a wait on this event for the Warp stream current during the first fetch-operation result access. It does not block the host, and no other stream is ordered, so the caller must establish its own Warp stream dependency before using the array elsewhere. The handle stays valid until the read session is released. Do not destroy it.

Type:

int

class ovphysx.api.WriteSession(
sdk,
query: int,
write: int,
groups=None,
native=None,
*,
metadata=None,
attributes=(),
stage=None,
attachment=None,
object_type=None,
)#

A completed write session; fetch, commit and close return uncollected operations.

Fill fetched groups in place and commit each explicitly. A successful earlier commit remains applied when a later commit fails; an accepted failed commit may have partially applied rows and must never be retried. Caller commit order determines command/property ordering. The caller’s Query is not owned here. Group arrays are borrowed: do not access them after commit admission or close.

close() → Operation[None]#

Submit release. Rejected admission leaves ownership available for retry.

Finish CUDA fills of uncommitted groups first; close takes no producer synchronization handles.

commit(
group: WriteGroup,
cuda_stream: int = 0,
cuda_wait_event: int = 0,
*,
event_owner=None,
) → Operation[None]#

Submit a filled group’s publication, spending it on admission.

Complete host fills before calling. For outstanding CUDA fills, pass the producer stream, completion event, or both; both dependencies are honored when supplied. They do not select PhysX’s execution stream. Only two zero handles assert that no producer work remains, even for host-resident data. Stream 1 names the legacy default stream in the caller’s current CUDA context; make the producer context current when using this sentinel.

Keep supplied streams and events valid through commit completion. Pass event_owner to retain their Python owner, or a tuple of owners, through collection. The current native implementation may block this call while completing producer dependencies. A successful task confirms CPU mutation or GPU submission; GPU execution can continue afterward. Synchronization errors fail the task and the admitted group remains spent.

fetch_next() → Operation[WriteGroup | None]#

Submit one fetch. A successful result of None is end of iteration.

release() → Operation[None]#

Submit release. Rejected admission leaves ownership available for retry.

Finish CUDA fills of uncommitted groups first; close takes no producer synchronization handles.
